title: A Small Nonhalting Probability
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a type, and let $r$ map bit strings to either an element of $\alpha$ or no value. Suppose that whenever $r(w)$ has a value, appending any bit string to $w$ leaves that value unchanged. Assume there is a rational bound $B$ such that for every nonnegative integer $K$, the sum, over $0\le t<K$, of the probability that $r$ has no value on a uniformly random $t$-bit string is at most $B$. Then for every rational $\varepsilon>0$, some nonnegative integer $t$ has probability at most $\varepsilon$ that $r$ has no value on a uniformly random $t$-bit string.
hypotheses_covered: $r$ maps bit strings to an optional value in $\alpha$
Any extension of a string on which $r$ has a value has the same value
For every $K$, the sum of nonhalting probabilities for $0\le t<K$ is at most the rational number $B$
